title: Partial KV-cache legacy state caused chat degradation - incident log
summary: During a staged model rollout to a new 8-bit quantized variant, a subset of chat serving nodes retained an older KV cache layout. This caused increased hallucinations and truncated multi-turn context on ~12% of traffic routed to the canary cohort. The issue surfaced within 18 minutes of rollout start and required an immediate rollback of the canary and a coordinated cache-invalidation hotfix to restore normal behavior.
impact: Approximately 12% of production chat requests (canary cohort) experienced content degradation: off-topic responses, repeated tokens, and occasional early EOS. No data leakage or PII exposure observed. User-visible errors returned <0.1% of requests. Customer-facing SLAs were not breached, but internal SLOs for model quality on canaries were violated.
detection: Alert: mean_chat_quality_score_canary dropped from 0.92 to 0.63 over 10 minutes at 2025-11-03T14:08Z. Pager notified oncall SRE Marcus Liu. Slack thread #ops-incidents received multiple developer reports about odd multi-turn truncation. Automated canary divergence check (eval-set perplexity delta) flagged >20% relative regression.
timeline:
2025-11-03T13:52Z - Staged rollout started to canary cohort (5% traffic) with model v2-quant-8b.
2025-11-03T14:05Z - First automated divergence alert (perplexity delta).
2025-11-03T14:08Z - mean_chat_quality_score alert and pager. Oncall engaged.
2025-11-03T14:12Z - Initial hypothesis: quantized weights causing sampling shift. SRE and Applied ML started parallel checks.
2025-11-03T14:18Z - Quick-check: weight checksums and manifests matched expected versions on most nodes.
2025-11-03T14:25Z - Deep inspection of routing logs revealed a subpopulation of nodes still serving with previous KV cache metadata format (legacy layout v0) despite model binary swap.
2025-11-03T14:30Z - Canary traffic reduced to 0% (automatic safety rollback) but degraded responses persisted on some regional shards.
2025-11-03T14:36Z - Coordinated hotfix deployed: forced cache invalidation and staged node restart for affected pool.
2025-11-03T14:50Z - Telemetry shows recovery of mean_chat_quality_score to baseline for all cohorts.
2025-11-03T15:10Z - Post-rollback validation completed; service returned to normal.
mitigation: Immediate actions: (1) reduced canary traffic to 0% to stop further exposure, (2) triggered cache-invalidation job targeting the affected shard range, (3) restarted serving pods in the impacted node pool to reclaim consistent KV layout, (4) verified model checksum, tokenizer version, and cache metadata versions post-restart. The combination of invalidation + restart restored correct behavior.
root_cause: A non-atomic incremental model rollout did a binary weight swap while leaving a stale KV cache metadata format on a subset of GPU serving instances. The new model binary expected a slightly different KV metadata header (added version field), and when combined with legacy cache entries the runtime produced incorrect KV lookups for prefix caching leading to truncated context and token duplication.
contributing_factors: Manifest TTL/propagation lag: manifest update propagated before cache-metadata compatibility tags were fully honored by the rollout orchestration.
Partial restart policy: orchestration used a lazy in-place model replace on some nodes (no full restart), leaving cache blobs intact.
Inadequate preflight: preflight checks validated model checksum but did not validate runtime KV metadata version compatibility across serving nodes.
Monitoring blind spot: no explicit metric tracked 'kv_cache_format_mismatch_count' or 'kv_lookup_miss_pattern' to quickly catch mismatched formats.
Sampling bias: canary sampling routed particularly to an older regional pool due to a transient topology preference, increasing impact.
action_items: SRE-2147: Add preflight check to verify KV cache metadata version across all serving instances before promoting model manifest (owner: Marcus Liu, due: 2025-11-10)
SERV-PR-5298: Change default rollout step to include an atomic cache-flush hook when swapping model binaries (owner: Diego Ramirez, due: 2025-11-08)
Improve monitoring: add 'kv_cache_format_mismatch_count' and 'kv_lookup_anomaly' derived metrics + dashboards (owner: Hannah Kim, due: 2025-11-12)
Run a simulated partial-restart chaos test during next staging deploys to verify lazy-replace invariants (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2025-11-20)
Update runbooks: explicit rollback play for cache-metadata mismatches and a pre-deployment checklist (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2025-11-06)
Postmortem review with Applied ML to add compatibility testing for KV layout changes in model onboarding pipeline (owner: Marcus Liu + Applied ML, due: 2025-11-17)
runbook_changes: Add a new section: 'Model swap cache compatibility verification' with commands to check kv_metadata_version across nodes and to force global cache invalidation.
Add emergency CLI commands to drain a pool, run 'kvcache-check --target-pool', and to schedule rolling restarts with a cache-flush window.
Adjust automated rollout pipeline to pause and require manual confirmation if manifest propagation difference across AZs > 5 seconds.
Add one-click rollback button in Console that triggers simultaneous: reduce-canary->drain-pool->global-cache-flush->verify-metrics.
Document symptoms for oncall: high kv_lookup_failure_rate, sudden spike in duplicate token counts, drop in canary quality score.
retrospective_notes: This incident highlights a brittle assumption: the runtime tolerated mismatched cache metadata silently rather than failing fast. Moving forward we should favor explicit compatibility checks and fail-fast semantics during model swaps. The quick detection came from our canary quality metric — keep that signal and improve coverage. Communication across orchestration, runtime, and model-onboarding teams needs a short shared checklist for any change that touches cache layout or binary metadata.
